---
title: "Rust: Axum"
description: "Add passwordless auth (passkeys, magic links, email and SMS codes) to a Rust Axum app without writing JWT code, with the official seamless-auth crate: install, a complete app, configuration, and cookie and bearer transport."
sidebar:
  order: 3.3
---

`seamless-auth` on crates.io is the official Seamless Auth server adapter for Rust and Axum. It
gives you an Axum router for the `/auth` routes the frontend SDKs call, a `require_auth()` tower
layer for your own routes, and a `User` extractor for the signed-in user. The session lives in
signed `HttpOnly` cookies on your own domain. You do not write token parsing, JWKS fetching, cookie
signing, or refresh logic.

Use it when your backend is Axum and you want passkeys, magic links, email or SMS codes, or OAuth
sign-in against a Seamless Auth server (self-hosted `seamless-auth-api` or a managed instance). It
is held to the same conformance suite as the Express, Fastify, Go, and Python adapters. For other
languages see [Server SDKs And Adapters](/build/server-sdks).

Source: [fells-code/seamless-auth-rust](https://github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-rust). Current
release: `0.2.0` (pre-1.0, so the public API may change between minor versions).

---

## Install

```bash
cargo add seamless-auth
cargo add axum@0.8 serde_json
cargo add tokio@1 --features macros,rt-multi-thread,net
```

It needs Rust 1.88 or later and Axum 0.8. The crate name is `seamless_auth`.

| Feature      | Default | Purpose                                              |
| ------------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `rustls`     | yes     | TLS to the auth API with rustls                      |
| `native-tls` | no      | TLS to the auth API with the platform's TLS library |

With neither, the adapter reaches the auth API over plain HTTP only.

---

## A Complete App

This mounts the auth routes at `/auth`, protects `/api/me`, and reads the current user. It follows
the reference app the conformance suite drives (`conformance/refapp/main.rs`).

```rust
use std::net::SocketAddr;

use axum::{Json, Router, routing::get};
use seamless_auth::{Adapter, User};
use serde_json::json;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut builder = Adapter::builder(std::env::var("AUTH_SERVER_URL")?)
        .cookie_secret(std::env::var("COOKIE_SIGNING_KEY")?) // 32 bytes or more
        .service_secret(std::env::var("API_SERVICE_TOKEN")?) // the auth API's API_SERVICE_TOKEN
        .jwks_kid(std::env::var("JWKS_KID")?);
    if let Ok(issuer) = std::env::var("AUTH_SERVER_ISSUER") {
        builder = builder.auth_server_issuer(issuer);
    }
    let auth = builder.build()?;

    let app = Router::new()
        // Your own route, behind the adapter's guard. require_auth answers 401 without a session.
        .route(
            "/api/me",
            get(|user: User| async move { Json(json!({ "id": user.id, "roles": user.roles })) })
                .route_layer(auth.require_auth()),
        )
        // The auth routes, at /auth, which is where the frontend SDKs call.
        .nest("/auth", auth.router());

    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("0.0.0.0:8080").await?;
    // Connect info gives the adapter the peer address to forward to the auth API.
    axum::serve(
        listener,
        app.into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>(),
    )
    .await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

- `Adapter::builder(url)` takes the auth API URL; `.build()` returns a `BuildError` on an invalid
  URL or a secret shorter than 32 bytes, so a misconfigured app fails to boot.
- `auth.router()` serves every auth route. Nest it at `/auth`.
- `auth.require_auth()` is a tower layer. It answers 401 `{"error":"unauthenticated"}` unless the
  request carries a session, and puts a `User` in the request extensions, which handlers take as an
  extractor.
- `User` has `id`, `roles`, `email`, `phone` (both `Option<String>`), and `token` (the auth API
  access token). On a bearer request `email` and `phone` are `None`, because the access token does
  not carry them.
- Serve with `into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>()`. Without it the adapter has no
  peer address and forwards no client address to the auth API.

There is no role layer in the crate. Check `user.roles` in your handler. For a web app on another
origin, add credentialed CORS for that origin (for example `tower-http`'s `CorsLayer`).

## Configuration

The adapter reads no environment variables itself. The names below are the ones the Seamless
starters, the conformance reference app, and `seamless init` use, so a project the CLI wrote
already has them in `.env`.

| Variable             | Builder method          | Value                                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `AUTH_SERVER_URL`    | `Adapter::builder(url)` | Where your server reaches the auth API, for example `http://localhost:5312`, or the Auth Server URL from the portal |
| `AUTH_SERVER_ISSUER` | `auth_server_issuer`    | Only when the auth API signs as a different URL (the `seamless init --local` Docker stack signs as `http://auth:5312`) |
| `COOKIE_SIGNING_KEY` | `cookie_secret`         | Any secret of 32 bytes or more, for example `openssl rand -base64 48`                                               |
| `API_SERVICE_TOKEN`  | `service_secret`        | The auth API's `API_SERVICE_TOKEN` (self-hosted), or a service token generated in the portal (managed)              |
| `JWKS_KID`           | `jwks_kid`              | `kid` header on the service tokens the adapter signs, not the auth API's signing key id; `dev-main` on a local stack |

The builder also has:

| Builder method                         | Default                                  | Purpose                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `audience`                             | the issuer                               | Expected `aud` of the auth API's tokens                                                  |
| `cookie_domain`                        | none                                     | Cookie `Domain`                                                                          |
| `insecure_cookies`                     | `false`                                  | Drops `Secure`, for local development over plain HTTP on a host other than `localhost`  |
| `same_site`                            | `None`, or `Lax` with `insecure_cookies` | Cookie `SameSite`                                                                        |
| `allowed_origins`                      | none                                     | The only cross-origin callers allowed to change state while cookies are `SameSite=None` |
| `session_cookie_names`                 | `seamless-access`, `seamless-refresh`    | Session cookie names                                                                     |
| `flow_cookie_names`                    | `seamless-ephemeral`                     | Sign-in flow cookie names                                                                |
| `deliver`                              | none                                     | Send OTP codes and magic links through your own transports                               |
| `trusted_proxies`, `resolve_client_ip` | the connecting peer                      | The end user's address; use `TrustedProxies::new(["10.0.0.0/8"])?` behind a proxy       |
| `disable_manifest_fetch`               | `false`                                  | Use only the manifest embedded in this version                                           |
| `http_client`                          | 15 second timeout, no redirects          | Outbound `reqwest::Client`                                                               |

### Delivering codes yourself

Without `deliver`, the auth API sends OTP codes and magic links. With it, the adapter asks the API
for the message and hands it to you as a `Delivery` (`kind`, `to`, and the optional `token`,
`magic_link_url`, and `sign_in_url`). A returned error answers 502 `delivery_failed`.

```rust
.deliver(move |d: seamless_auth::Delivery| {
    let mailer = mailer.clone();
    async move { mailer.send(&d.to, &d.kind, d.token.as_deref(), d.magic_link_url.as_deref()).await }
})
```

### Serving the admin console

`auth.console_router()` serves the Seamless admin dashboard at `/console` from your API, proxied
from the auth API. Merge it rather than nesting it, because a router nested at `/console` never sees
`/console/`:

```rust
let app = Router::new()
    .nest("/auth", auth.router())
    .merge(auth.console_router());
```

Add your API's origin to the auth server's `ORIGINS` so passkey ceremonies started in the console
verify.

---

## Cookie And Bearer Transport

The same `/auth` routes serve two contracts:

- **Browsers** get cookies. The adapter keeps the auth API's tokens in signed `HttpOnly` cookies
  and refreshes the session silently on the auth routes. Page scripts never see a token.
- **Native clients** (mobile apps, CLIs) send `x-seamless-auth-transport: bearer`. Session-issuing
  responses then return `token` and `refreshToken` in the body and set no cookie, and the client
  refreshes with `POST /auth/refresh` and `Authorization: Bearer <refreshToken>`.

`require_auth()` accepts either the session cookie or an auth API access token in
`Authorization: Bearer`, and the cookie wins when both are present. It reads the `Cookie` header
itself, so it works on any route, and it does not refresh. `auth.authenticate(&headers)` runs the
same check without answering the request.

While cookies are `SameSite=None`, a state-changing request the guard admits on the cookie from
another site (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, or an `Origin` outside `allowed_origins`) answers 403
`cross_site_request_blocked`. The auth routes only accept JSON request bodies (`application/json`
or a `+json` type); anything else answers 415 `unsupported_media_type`. The frontend SDKs already
send JSON.

See [Bearer Transport For Native Clients](/build/server-sdks#bearer-transport-for-native-clients)
for the full contract, which every adapter shares.

---

## How The Frontend Talks To It

Every frontend SDK calls `${apiHost}/auth/...`, so point it at this server's origin, for example
`<AuthProvider apiHost="http://localhost:8080">` in [React](/build/react-sdk). The same `apiHost`
option exists in [Angular](/build/angular-sdk), [Vue](/build/vue-sdk), [Svelte](/build/svelte-sdk),
and [React Native](/build/react-native-sdk). Browser requests to your own protected routes need
`credentials: 'include'` when the web app runs on another origin.

---

## Version Compatibility

| `seamless-auth` (crates.io) | Auth API         | Rust  | Axum |
| --------------------------- | ---------------- | ----- | ---- |
| 0.2.0                       | v0.18.0 or later | 1.88+ | 0.8  |

Which routes the adapter serves comes from the adapter manifest the auth API publishes at
`/.well-known/seamless-adapter.json`, first served by auth API v0.18.0, so a new API route works
without a new crate release. The adapter fetches it on the first request and keeps it for the life
of the process. If the API serves none, it falls back to the copy embedded in the crate. Run auth
API v0.18.0 or later: the adapter sends the OTP and magic-link send routes as `POST`, which v0.17.0
answers with 404. `seamless-cli` 0.21.0 scaffolds v0.17.0, so in a project it generated, bump the
`ghcr.io/fells-code/seamless-auth-api` image tag to `v0.18.0`.

---

## Conformance

The adapter is held to the adapter conformance suite in `seamless-cli`
([`verify/CONFORMANCE.md`](https://github.com/fells-code/seamless-cli/blob/main/verify/CONFORMANCE.md)),
the same suite the Express and Fastify adapters pass, in CI on every change. To run it yourself you
need Docker, a checkout of `seamless-auth-api`, and the `seamless` CLI:

```bash
PORT=8080 AUTH_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:5312 AUTH_SERVER_ISSUER=http://auth-api:5312 \
  API_SERVICE_TOKEN=verify-dev-service-token-not-a-real-secret \
  COOKIE_SIGNING_KEY=verify-dev-service-token-not-a-real-secret JWKS_KID=dev-main \
  cargo run --example refapp &

SEAMLESS_API_DIR=../seamless-auth-api seamless verify --adapter-url=http://localhost:8080
```

---

## Starter Template

`seamless-templates` has an Axum api starter (`templates/api/axum`, status beta) built on this
crate, which `seamless init` selects with `--axum` or `--api=axum`. It is on the templates `main`
branch and is not in a release yet: the published `seamless-cli` 0.21.0 pins templates `v0.17.0`
and scaffolds auth API v0.17.0, which this adapter does not support, so wait for the next CLI
release rather than pointing 0.21.0 at templates `main`.

---

## Do Not Write Your Own Token Verification

Use `require_auth()` or `authenticate` rather than decoding the session cookie or the access token
yourself. They check the cookie signature, the auth API's JWKS signature, issuer, audience, expiry,
and token type, and the layer adds the cross-site rules above. A hand-rolled `jsonwebtoken` check
usually misses one of those, and the cookie format is internal to the adapter.
